raw_context:
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)
involves tracking health data like blood glucose or blood pressure at home using connected medical devices, which automatically share readings with a clinical care team or pharmacy. While
specialized platforms like
ProCare Innovations
provide clinical RPM hardware for chronic disease management, retail or consumer devices such as smartwatches and sleep trackers offer personal wellness insights rather than direct medical-grade clinical reporting
Medhealth Outlook
How Pharmacy RPM Works
Device Setup:
Patients receive simple cellular or Bluetooth tools like blood glucose meters or blood pressure cuffs.
Data Transmission:
Readings transmit automatically to a secure portal reviewed by clinical pharmacists.
Intervention:
Out-of-range vital signs trigger automated alerts so care teams can adjust therapy or contact the patient's doctor.
Tenovi | Remote Patient Monitoring
Consumer Wearables vs. Clinical Tools
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Provide real-time interstitial glucose data, often integrated directly into diabetes care management.
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Offer spot-check heart rhythms and activity tracking, though consumer wrist-based non-invasive glucose features lack standard clinical-grade diagnostic accuracy.
Sleep Trackers:
Monitor resting heart rate and rest cycles for general lifestyle optimization.
